entries.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Make a new high-fidelity desktop conversation UI design for the Chinese companion app 在场, using the supplied app image only as the reference for its restrained warm ivory, soft window light, quiet gold, Chinese typography, generous content spacing, simple top navigation and small anime avatar. This is a design study, not a screenshot of a functioning app. Do not copy its two-column PDF layout. Create an integrated, editorially beautiful interactive explanation of how a GRAND PIANO makes and stops a sound, within an ordinary conversation. 1536x1024 landscape composition. Keep the actual app chrome: small door logo and 在场 upper left, subtle 聊天 / 今天 / 留下 pill centered, tiny companion avatar upper right; a compact conversational composer at the bottom. No large character covers the learning content. No developer labels or dashboard badges.
Design direction A: one continuous warm paper as an instrument, NOT a black/blue technical dashboard, no boxes inside boxes. At the top of the conversation show a small avatar with the name 澪, then one friendly short line '先轻轻按一下，再松开。'. Below is an ample softly textured off-white paper with the quiet serif heading '一枚琴键，怎样留住一个声音'. The main content is a beautiful, precise, readable vector-like side cutaway mechanism occupying most of the paper width: horizontal ivory key acting on a fulcrum, warm wooden wippen and jack, angled wooden hammer shank with rounded felt hammer head rising toward a horizontal string above, a separate felt damper resting above the string, and a bridge/soundboard at the right. Keep the lever connections and labels readable, mechanical details simplified clearly, not fantastical. Show the hammer detached and in flight just before striking, with one delicate gold motion arc; string turquoise/slate line, damper charcoal, wood honey gold. Small nearby Chinese labels '琴键', '顶杆', '琴槌', '琴弦', '制音器', '琴桥' with fine restrained leader lines. No dense Cartesian graph grid.
Immediately beneath this cutaway, on the SAME paper, place a playable-looking full C4 to C5 one-octave piano keyboard: eight ivory white keys, five matte charcoal black keys grouped correctly in two and three. The pressed C4 has a subtle gold edge and soft depressed depth. Keep the keyboard physically close to the mechanism so they feel causally related, not another disconnected card. Beside the keys, a small frequency reading 'C4 · 261.6 Hz', and a small restrained waveform trace. Beneath, a single slim control row with a '力度' gold slider, a '慢慢看' play control, a compact '延音' switch, and a quiet reset icon; a subtle speaker icon enables sound. At the active mechanism position place one short margin note '琴槌已经离开顶杆，继续向琴弦飞去。' in normal readable text, without a large status panel. Include a discreet four-stop process line '按下  ·  脱开  ·  击弦  ·  回弹', current stage highlighted naturally, no big progress percentage.
After the paper, the conversation continues with one short readable paragraph about releasing the key with the pedal off versus on; include the formula f₁ = (1/2L) √(T/μ) in elegant mathematical typography. The design must feel welcoming, calm, beautiful, intellectually serious, and genuinely touchable. Preserve clear text contrast, no text over the mechanism, no huge English headline, no extra permanent help banners, no boilerplate disclaimers, no AI implementation details. Show a realistic amount of content at usable desktop size, not an empty decorative hero. The cutaway and keys should be the visual focus, with the app identity felt through materials and spacing.

entries.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create a second substantially different, implementable design study for the Chinese desktop companion app 在场. Use the attached app image as the style reference: warm ivory, natural window light, muted gold, beautiful legible Chinese serif learning text, refined sparse controls, small avatar, calm app navigation. A 1536x1152 landscape app screen. This study is a CONVERSATIONAL EXPLORABLE EXPLANATION, with two genuinely interactive paper sections separated by the companion's prose. Keep the small 在场 door logo upper left and 聊天 / 今天 / 留下 navigation at the top, small avatar top right, compact composer at the bottom. The drawings must look like precise, elegant SVG illustrations that can actually move and be recalculated, not photorealistic renders or painted assets. No black/blue dashboard, no dark cards, no full character illustration, no decorative status panels.
Direction B: an open illustrated notebook. One quiet prose line from 澪 introduces the first experiment. First paper section heading '先看琴槌怎样碰到琴弦'. The generous flat diagram shows a simplified grand piano action side view, correctly separated into key lever on fulcrum, wippen/jack linkage, angled hammer shank and felt hammer head BELOW a horizontal string, separate felt damper ABOVE that string, and bridge at right. Clean honey wood strokes, warm gray outlines, small teal/slate vibrating string, subtle amber accent on the currently moving lever. Plenty of white paper between parts; no dense grid. The jack stops pushing BEFORE impact and the hammer head is in free flight below the string. Tiny labels with leader lines only at the relevant parts. Directly below this diagram are a small scrubbable timeline and quiet controls '慢慢看', '下一步', '复位'; a single-key lever at the left looks pressable, not a row of explanatory cards. One small in-paper margin sentence explains the current stage. This is a visual explanation of force and release, not a decorative full piano.
Between the two paper sections, ordinary companion prose says '再听听看：松开琴键以后，声音为什么还在？' in the same reading flow, with no extra author bubble border. Second paper section is compact and tactile: a playable C4–C5 keyboard beneath an elegant thin wave/envelope line, followed by a single row '力度' slider, '延音' switch and small sound toggle. EXACT KEY GEOMETRY: 8 white keys labeled C4 D4 E4 F4 G4 A4 B4 C5. EXACTLY 5 black keys: C-sharp BETWEEN white C4 and D4, D-sharp BETWEEN D4 and E4, then NO black between E4/F4; F-sharp BETWEEN F4/G4, G-sharp BETWEEN G4/A4, A-sharp BETWEEN A4/B4, then NO black between B4/C5. Two-black group then three-black group, never a black key on every gap. Keys are quiet ivory and warm charcoal, one C4 white key softly pressed with a muted gold lower edge. Normal note readout 'C4 · 261.6 Hz' is small. No giant labels or simulation scores.
The lower conversation can continue with a small formula f₁ = (1/2L) √(T/μ) and one brief explanation, visually part of the conversation rather than a third card. Keep mechanical diagram, keyboard, controls and narration all readable at realistic desktop scale; the first experiment explains mechanism, the second lets the person hear the sustain distinction. Soft paper texture should be almost imperceptible. Gentle fine borders and tiny shadows, warm coherent neutrals, clear contrast. Preserve the feeling of sitting together at a study desk. No software implementation language, no arbitrary code blocks, no repeated helper text for each control, no title saying Interactive Lab. Do not create photorealistic mechanical hardware; this design must be feasible as live vector geometry and native controls.
